public_prompt: The reconciler compares the sum of 4.2M ledger line amounts against the bank total and reports a gap of 1,842 currency units. The working position: the gap is small, so accept a 0.01% tolerance and close the month. Report the true total and account for the gap.
observable_resources: ledger/lines.csv — 4,200,000 amounts carrying two fractional digits, read into and summed as 64-bit floating point
ledger/repro.md — summing the same file in a different row order changes the total by up to 2,300 currency units
ledger/bank-statement.csv — the bank total is a whole number of minor currency units and is identical on every re-read
ledger/spot-check.md — 40 sampled lines reconcile to the last minor unit when added by hand
closure:month-end-signoff-march — closed; accepts the gap under a 0.01% tolerance
closure:ledger-retention-standard — closed; keeps line records for 7 years; rests on the statutory requirement, not on any total computed from them

protected_gold.root_success_rubric: PASS iff the answer attributes the gap to accumulated rounding in the floating-point sum, cites the order dependence as the demonstration, and recomputes the total over whole minor units or an exact fractional type so that it matches the bank figure with no tolerance at all. FAIL if the answer keeps the tolerance, sorts the lines before summing, sums in a different order, or attributes the gap to missing or duplicated rows.

source_provenance: no external dataset; every figure is authored for this benchmark and is not an empirical finding
notes: A solver that keeps the tolerance framing closes the month on a gap that is a property of the arithmetic rather than of the ledger, and the order dependence proves it.
